subject: General Science
title: Chemical Families

outcomes.text: identify chemical families in the periodic table,
classify elements of the periodic table into their chemical families,
investigate the physical and chemical properties of selected elements of the periodic table,
outline the uses of elements of the periodic table,
appreciate the uses of the elements of the periodic table in day-to-day life.

content: Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals
Physical and chemical properties of selected elements
Uses of the elements and their compounds
inquiry_questions: How are elements suited to their use in day-to-day life?
suggested_learning_experiences: Search for information on the categories of elements in the periodic table (alkali, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals).
Sort and group the first twenty elements of the periodic table into their families.
Discuss with peers selected transition elements of the periodic table (copper, iron, zinc, lead).
Observe safety when carrying out activities to investigate properties of elements of the periodic table. Appropriately use first aid kits in case of injuries.
Carry out activities to investigate physical properties of alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals.
Carry out activities to investigate the reaction of sodium, magnesium and chlorine with air (oxygen), water and dilute acids where applicable (write balanced chemical equations for the reactions).
Discuss with peers the properties of elements of the periodic table in relation to their uses.
Discuss with peers how noble gases are suited to their applications in day-to-day life.
Discuss with peers the properties of elements that make them suitable for use in illuminating roads.
Use available digital and print media to research on transition elements and their uses.
coreCompetencies:
Self-efficacy: as the learner carries out activities to investigate the reaction of sodium, magnesium and chlorine with air and dilute acids.
Digital literacy: as the learner uses available digital and print media to research on transition elements and their uses.
values: Love: as the learner takes care of self and others by observing safety when carrying out activities to investigate properties of elements of the periodic table and appropriately using first aid kits in case of injuries.
pcis: Road safety: as the learner discusses with peers the properties of elements that make them suitable for use in illuminating roads.

notes: No lesson allocation is stated in this table; do not use the inventory baseline count as an official allocation.

The source names sodium, magnesium, chlorine, air, water and dilute acids. Sodium–water, chlorine-related and acid reactions require formal specialist risk assessment, trained supervision, appropriate controls and local approval. Safer learner work may use teacher-prepared results, models or approved low-risk demonstrations; no learner handling of sodium or chlorine or uncontrolled gas generation.
Physical properties can be investigated through approved specimens or reference data. The source does not authorize unsupervised chemical handling or infer that any investigation was performed.
